classification.difficultyReason: Directly interpret absolute value as distance, first from zero and then from the specified centre b; no equation solving is required.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Give a definition of $|x|=a$ as a distance on the number line.

answer.short: The distance of $x$ from the origin is $a$.
answer.worked: $|x|$ is the distance of $x$ from zero. Thus $|x|=a$ means that this distance is $a$. For $a\geq0$, the positions are $-a$ and $a$; when $a=0$, they coincide. A negative distance gives no solution.

spec.sourceRegion: Answer book PDF page 26, printed page 320, Exercise 4A F4(a)
spec.description: Horizontal symbolic number line below the answer sentence, with two outward curved distance arrows from zero, each labelled a. Template coordinates normalise symbolic positions; they are not numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: For a>0, -a and a are each distance a from zero.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Give a definition of $|x-b|=a$ as a distance on the number line.

answer.worked: $|x-b|$ is the distance between $x$ and $b$. Thus $|x-b|=a$ means that this distance is $a$. For $a\geq0$, the positions are $b-a$ and $b+a$; when $a=0$, both are $b$. A negative distance gives no solution.

spec.sourceRegion: Answer book PDF page 26, printed page 320, Exercise 4A F4(b)
spec.description: Horizontal symbolic number line below the answer sentence, with two outward curved distance arrows from b, each labelled a. Template coordinates normalise symbolic positions; they are not numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: For a>0, b-a and b+a are each distance a from b.
